name: lp2lp
setup: [z, p, k] = buttap(4); [bp, ap] = zp2tf(z, p, k);
expr: [bt, at] = lp2lp(bp, ap, 100); r1 = double(numel(bt) + numel(at)); b1 = bt(1); a2 = at(2); a5 = at(5);
comment: Sig: [bt,at] = lp2lp(b,a,Wo) -- TF form. DEEP-PROBE 2026-05-31: numerator length now matches MATLAB. The 4th-order Butterworth prototype has NO zeros, so MATLAB returns bt at its true degree (length 1, = Wo^4) NOT zero-padded to the denominator length 5. Root cause was twofold: tf2zp computed the ZPK gain from b(1) (=0 for a zero-padded numerator like [0 0 0 0 1]) instead of the first nonzero coeff, and the lp2* TF dispatch left zp2tf's padding in place. Now: numel(bt)+numel(at)=6 (was 10), bt(1)=1e8, at(2)=261.312592975, at(5)=1e8. namespace=signal. Matches MATLAB R2025b.
